conclusions: Only a private WeakSet of fully validated resolver-owned recursively frozen outputs can bypass library validation. Originals, edited clones, shallow/deep frozen foreign objects and proxies do not inherit its identity.
Branding does not provide catalogue authority or change effective permissions, same-hash restrictions, upload capacity or malformed-input validation.

The player retains one cache entry. Keys are its owned immutable library identity, owned copied context identity and primitive override. The entry is replaced only after selection resolution succeeds.

Null catalogue and existing resolver-branded catalogues permit memoization. Raw adapters are never memoized, even when their root is frozen; subsequent policy mutations and malformed edits are still observed.
Published allowed(), failed track membership and authored fallback remain outside the memo. Snapshot status/position/queue and transport intent are not cached.
Context updates remain replacement based. Library/listening/installed IDs/recording-mode/override updates select new dependencies; existing invalid setter validation leaves old valid state intact.
Constructor catalogue validation now occurs before media deck/master ownership. Invalid input leaves no media-owner or subscription residue, allowing a clean retry.
The seven existing menu tests and their deadlines are byte-identical to baseline. No timeout increase or removal of behavioral assertions is part of this optimization.
